newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's Bucaram is still in the money.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Bucaram is still in the money.

text.p: Ecuador's Abdala Bucaram was booted out of the ornate Carondelet presidential palace last week but the flamboyant, self-styled "man of the people" has a lifetime right to remain on its payroll.
As former head of state, Bucaram will be entitled from 1998 to claim a monthly salary based on the sitting president's current wage.
Without fringe benefits it will probably be lower than the eight million sucres ($2,150) Bucaram was receiving until he was ousted by Congress last week, parliamentary sources said.
But it is a tidy sum in a country where the average wage earner takes home less than $100 a month.
Critics said the populist leader, whose rule only lasted six months, was in no need of state money since he amassed a fortune through alleged corruption and allegedly shady business deals.
Dismissing such accusations as slander from "jealous oligarchs," Bucaram has always said he honestly earned his money.
During provincial tours in recent months, Bucaram, always the champion of the poor, on various occasions donated his own salary and that of government ministers to impoverished people.
In January during a visit to Panama he gave $80,000 which he said was from his own pocket to residents of a Panama City poor neighbourhood.
